17: MATRYÓNA. But you just hear what Iván Moséitch bids us do. “Above all,” he says, “mind and don't let the money slip away, dame. If she don't get hold of the money,” he says, “they'll not let her do it. Money's the great thing!” So look out, sonnie, things are coming to a head.
16: NIKÍTA. This paper's only a decision for the elders to sign. There's no great wisdom needed for that.
15: NIKÍTA [ laughs ] That goes without saying, only fork out the money. Who does not want money? MATRYÓNA. Well then, honey, so I spoke out plainly about the affair. And he says, “First and foremost, your son will have to get himself on the register of that village—that will cost something. The elders will have to be treated. And they, you see, they'll sign. Everything,” says he, “must be done sensibly.” Look, [ unwraps her kerchief and takes out a paper ] he's written out this paper; just read it, you're a scholar, you know. [ Nikíta reads ].
14: NIKÍTA. And what's it you've been bothering about?
12: MATRYÓNA [ keeps looking towards the porch while she speaks ] Eh, sonnie! Those that are alive have to think about living. One needs plenty of sense in these matters, honey. What do you think? I've tramped all over the place after your affairs, I've got quite footsore bothering about matters. And you must not forget me when the time comes.
11: MATRYÓNA. The old man will probably die to-day. NIKÍTA. Well, if he dies, God give him rest! What's that to me?
10: MATRYÓNA. Why, this affair—how you're to live your life. NIKÍTA. How to live my life? Others live, and I shall live!
9: MATRYÓNA [ approaches Nikíta ] Now then, sonnie. [ Sits down beside him ] Your affairs must also be thought about, and not left anyhow. NIKÍTA. What affairs?
8: ANÍSYA. Oh my head, my poor head! [ Exit ].
7: ANÍSYA. I don't know what to do; I know nothing, my brain's all in a whirl. Nan! Go, daughter, and see to the calves, they'll have run away, I'm afraid.… Oh dear, I haven't the courage. MATRYÓNA. Go on! I should think the samovár's boiling over.
6: ANÍSYA. Coming! What shall we do? MATRYÓNA. There's plenty of time if you do as I tell you.
5: ANÍSYA. Well? NAN. She was down in her daughter's vegetable plot—she's coming.
4: MATRYÓNA [ catches him by the arm ] Stay here, I tell you. Nan enters.
3: NIKÍTA. What is it? MATRYÓNA. You stay here—sit down—in case something is wanted.
2: MATRYÓNA. Don't talk about it I tell you, do as I bid you. Nikíta!
1: MATRYÓNA. Don't be talking now, but look alive, and I'll keep his sister off if need be. Mind, don't make a blunder! Get hold of the money and bring it here, and Nikíta will hide it. ANÍSYA. Oh my head, my head! I don't know how I'm going to …
